designNarrative: The implementation adds line-drawing to ReagentMapView.vue by extending the file's existing per-entity Cesium pattern: a single LEFT_CLICK handler registered once in onMounted resolves a screen click to a geographic point via camera.pickEllipsoid followed by an EllipsoidalOccluder visibility check (two independent guard clauses implementing the off-globe and far-side rejection paths), accumulates up to two draft points as component-local refs, and tags every entity -- including the two new draft kinds -- through one shared typed tagEntity() helper that replaces the previous per-call-site untyped cast. All new state and logic stay in the same file and layer as the code they extend, with no new module, store, or persisted state, exactly as architecture-notes.md decided. Behaviour change: yes.

findings.smell: addDraftPointEntity (line 213) and addDraftLineEntity (line 222) reach straight for viewer!, cesium!, ellipsoid! non-null assertions, while flyToSite (line 194) and pickLandPoint (line 242) -- the file's own established convention -- both open with an explicit `if (!viewer || !cesium || !ellipsoid) return` guard clause. The two new functions are only safe today because handleMapClick only calls placePoint (which calls them) after pickLandPoint has already confirmed all three are non-null -- an invariant that holds by the current call chain but isn't visible locally in either function.
findings.instruction: Either pass viewer/cesium/ellipsoid into addDraftPointEntity/addDraftLineEntity as already-narrowed parameters from placePoint, or add the same `if (!viewer || !cesium || !ellipsoid) return null` guard used elsewhere in this file and widen the return type to `CesiumModule.Entity | null`. Non-blocking: the current invariant is sound and the functions are small enough that the risk is low, but matching the house convention removes the implicit cross-function dependency.
